turns.question: I'm starting to think seriously about retiring but I honestly don't know where to begin. What should I be thinking about?
turns.answer:
Start with these points:

- **Your eligibility.** At age 56 with **21.5 years of service**, Section 11-130 reaches employees age 55 or older but under 60 who have at least 10 years of service. For employees with **20 or more years**, it provides an age-and-service annuity based on the accumulated employee and city contributions. [40 ILCS 5/11-130]

- **The age-60 difference.** Section 11-134 provides retirement formulas for employees with 20 or more years of service. One available formula is **2.40% for each year of service** based on the highest average annual salary for four consecutive years within the last 10 years, subject to an **80% maximum**. If the annuity begins before age 60, that formula includes a reduction of **0.25% for each full month or fractional part** before age 60. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

- **Your salary record.** The salary basis matters greatly. Article 11 generally uses the highest average annual salary for four consecutive years within the last 10 years for the Section 11-134 formula. Overtime is not included, and Article 11 has specific rules for determining annual salary. [40 ILCS 5/11-134] [40 ILCS 5/11-217]

- **Your service record.** Service credit can include actual service, certain paid or short unpaid leaves, and certain disability periods. Overtime or extra service is excluded, and no more than one year of service is allowed for service rendered during a calendar year. [40 ILCS 5/11-215] [40 ILCS 5/11-216]

The practical comparison is retiring now versus continuing to age 60. Retiring now may mean an earlier annuity but may also involve the before-age-60 reduction. Continuing to work may add service and could change the salary average used in the calculation. The Code also contains other annuity provisions, including the age-and-service provision in Section 11-129, but that applies to withdrawal at age 60 or older and under 65, so it does not reach you at age 56. [40 ILCS 5/11-129]

I’m going by your record, which places you in Article 11 — tell me if that’s not right. The statute text available here does not establish every detail needed to determine whether any additional service credit or refund-related rule affects your situation.

cases.name: A survivor question that uses none of the survivor vocabulary

turns.question: My wife is worried about what happens to her if something happens to me. What would she get?
turns.answer:
If you die while still employed, your wife may qualify for a survivor annuity under Article 11. Because you have 21.5 years of service, the statute provides an eligible spouse an annuity equal to 50% of the minimum formula annuity earned and accrued to your credit at the time of death. This option requires that your marriage have been in effect for 10 full years or more. It is not reduced because of your age or your wife’s age. [40 ILCS 5/11-145.1]

The statute also provides other widow-annuity rules, including an annuity equal to one-half of the annuity you would have been entitled to receive if you withdrew the day before your death. Those rules include age and service conditions and may involve a reduction based on your wife’s age. The Code does not provide enough information here to determine that amount. [40 ILCS 5/11-145.1]

If you die without an annuity having been paid to you and your widow, any remaining accumulated employee contributions may instead be refunded to your designated beneficiary. If there is no surviving designated beneficiary, the statute lists your children and then your estate as the next recipients. [40 ILCS 5/11-166]

I'm going by your record, which places you in Article 11 — tell me if that's not right.

turns.question: Does any of this get taxed, and do I still get health insurance?
turns.answer:
Your pension annuity is generally subject to federal income-tax withholding. Illinois generally does not tax retirement income, but the Pension Code sections in front of me do not establish your personal federal tax treatment.

Health insurance is not guaranteed by Article 11. The Fund may allow you to assign part of your annuity to pay premiums for an available hospital or medical plan for you, your spouse, and children. The Board may also end that assignment option. [40 ILCS 5/11-223.1] The Code does not establish that your current health coverage automatically continues after retirement.
